lines.text: Triangles are on every SAT. Let's learn their key angle rules in a minute.
Every triangle has three interior angles: A, B, and C.
Line them up along a parallel through the top vertex, and they form a straight angle: A plus B plus C always equals one eighty.
Now extend the base past vertex C. That outside corner is an exterior angle, d.
Notice that C and d also sit on a straight line, so they add to one eighty too. That means the exterior angle d equals A plus B.
Here is how it saves time. If A is fifty-two degrees and B is seventy-one, skip angle C. Just add fifty-two and seventy-one: one twenty-three degrees.
On harder SAT problems, the angles are expressions: A is two x plus twelve, B is x plus nineteen, and the exterior angle is one twenty-one.
Set A plus B equal to the exterior angle: three x plus thirty-one equals one twenty-one. Three x is ninety, so x equals thirty.
Practice it on real SAT problems in SAT Math Learner.
